THOUGHT: The patient has a very large (>5 cm) bilobed sellar mass with suprasellar extension producing bitemporal hemianopia, optic atrophy, nonreactive pupils, and central hypopituitarism (hypothyroidism, hypogonadism with decreased libido/ED). The serum prolactin is massively elevated at 8,094 ng/mL. Prolactin levels this high (well above the usual stalk-effect threshold ~<200–300 ng/mL and far above the >1000 ng/mL commonly seen with true prolactin-secreting tumors) strongly point to a prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma. The imaging description (“bilobed/snowman” sellar mass with cavernous sinus invasion and ICA encasement) is classic for an invasive macroadenoma. The size (>5 cm) qualifies this as a giant prolactinoma. Other sellar/parasellar lesions (nonfunctioning macroadenoma with stalk effect, craniopharyngioma, meningioma, metastasis) remain possible but are far less likely given the prolactin magnitude and typical adenoma imaging/invasion pattern.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Giant prolactinoma (invasive prolactin-secreting pituitary macroadenoma) — most likely
2. Nonfunctioning pituitary macroadenoma causing elevated prolactin by stalk effect (less likely given extremely high PRL)
3. Invasive/aggressive non‑prolactin pituitary adenoma (e.g., null‑cell or gonadotroph macroadenoma) with mass effect
4. Suprasellar craniopharyngioma (less likely — would usually have cystic/calcified components and lower PRL)
5. Sellar/parasellar meningioma (or metastatic lesion to the pituitary) (least likely given hormone profile and imaging features)
